Nasa’s first manned Moon mission in more than 50 years that will take astronauts deeper into space than any human has gone before has blasted off.

The 322-foot rocket, carrying four crew members, successfully launched from Cape Canaveral in Florida at 6.36pm local time (11.36pm BST).

The four astronauts reached orbit ahead of circling the Earth for about 25 hours before catapulting towards the moon.

Five minutes into the flight, Commander Reid Wiseman said: “We have a beautiful moonrise, we’re headed right at it.”

The elite team had entered the capsule several hours earlier where they will remain for the next 10 days with about as much room as a small camper van.

Prior to them boarding, more than 700,000 gallons of fuel (2.6 million litres) was loaded into the spacecraft.

As they headed to the launch pad, the three Americans and one Canadian waved and shaped their hands into hearts to well-wishers.

Commander Reid Wiseman shouted to the crowd: “It’s a great day for us. It’s a great day for this team.”

The so-called lunar flyby around the Moon will send the crew some 252,000 miles (406,000 kilometres) into space before returning to Earth.

The current record for the furthest spaceflight is about 248,000 miles, held by members of the Apollo 13 lunar mission in 1970, which was hit by technical problems.

As they pass approximately 4,600 miles beyond the far side of the Moon, the Orion module will lose communication with the Earth for up to 50 minutes.

While the astronauts will not touch down on the satellite, the Artemis II mission paves the way for a future lunar landing and also lays the foundation to send a crew to Mars.

The UK is playing a part in the mammoth technical operation, with the Goonhilly Earth Station, near Helston, Cornwall, helping to track the capsule on its epic celestial voyage.

The mission previously had to be postponed by two months because of hydrogen fuel leaks and clogged helium lines.

The last time Nasa sent astronauts to the Moon was as part of the Apollo 17 mission in 1972.

Nasa is seeking to return a crew to the lunar surface by 2028, before China does in about 2030.

Hailing the mission ahead of the launch, US President Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform: “We are WINNING, in Space, on Earth, and everywhere in between — Economically, Militarily, and now, BEYOND THE STARS.

“Nobody comes close! America doesn’t just compete, we DOMINATE, and the whole World is watching.

“God bless our incredible Astronauts, God bless NASA, and God bless the Greatest Nation ever to exist, the United States of America! President DONALD J. TRUMP”

Earlier, the King also conveyed his “heartfelt good wishes” to the astronauts along with an impassioned environmental plea.

The royal message was sent to crew member Colonel Jeremy Hansen, a former fighter pilot from Canada, where Charles is head of state.

In it, the environmentalist monarch expressed his hope the trip would renew people’s conviction “that we must learn from the lessons of how we have over-exploited and polluted our own planet”.

Amid the fresh space race, Charles said it was vital “that the Moon remains a beacon of peaceful scientific discovery rather than a theatre of exploitation”.

Back in 2023, the King launched the Astra Carta initiative aimed at promoting sustainable, ethical, and responsible space exploration.

In his letter to Col Hansen, Charles wrote: “You will, most certainly, reflect upon the fragile beauty of Earth as it rises above the lunar horizon, just as your predecessors did half a century ago.

“May that sight renew in you, and in all who follow your journey, the conviction that we must learn from the lessons of how we have over-exploited and polluted our own planet, and thus care for the universe, and all life contained within it, with reverence and a true sense of what is sacred.

“In an age when humanity’s reach into the stars grows ever bolder, it is vital that the Moon remains a beacon of peaceful scientific discovery rather than a theatre of exploitation.”

He added: “As you embark on this momentous endeavour, I send you and your fellow crew members my heartfelt good wishes.

“May the stars align in your favour, and may your safe return inspire countless others to uphold the values of sustainability, co-operation and wonder that the Astra Carta enshrines.”

News.title: Bompastor fury as hair pull goes unpunished in frantic end to Champions League tie
News.content:
McCabe pulled Thompson to the ground by her hair, leaving the Chelsea player upset just moments before Arsenal’s place in the semi-finals was confirmed by the final whistle. The incident happened just minutes after Sjoeke Nüsken scored in the 94th-minute to give Chelsea a brief glimmer of hope for a comeback.

Bompastor was still aggrieved in her TV interview with the BBC, arriving with phone in hand and a clip of the moment McCabe pulled Thompson’s hair asking the valid question: “Why do we have VAR?”.

She added: “I don’t want to speak to them [the officials] because it’s always the same story. Even if I go and speak to them, they will not give me a clear answer. It’s difficult for me because I don’t want to be the only one talking about this situation. Everyone needs to understand that’s the difference between being qualified and not being qualified. It has a big impact on players.”



McCabe, who has a track record of on-field incidents, took to Instagram after the final whistle to apologise, while the Arsenal players celebrated with music in their dressing room, with a message against a black background saying: “I just want to clarify that I was genuinely reaching for the shirt, I wouldn’t ever want to pull someone’s hair. Full respect to Thompson.”



However McCabe’s apology was dismissed by Bompastor, who insisted that the act itself was deliberate by the Arsenal full-back. She added: “She [Thompson] was crying. She’s trying her best on the pitch in both games and it is not good enough, when you are playing football and someone pulls your hair, it’s bad. Of course she was crying and emotional with the situation and the result.”

News.title: Marc Skinner calls on Manchester United to invest after ‘punch in the face’
News.content:
Manchester United head coach Marc Skinner says their elimination from the Champions League is the “punch in the face” the club needs to wake up to the gap in investment between themselves and their rivals.

United’s European journey ended at the quarter-final stage after they were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich in Germany, having lost the first leg 3-2 at Old Trafford last week.

The club’s exit from the competition came on the same day as the publication of their accounts for the 2024-25 season, which showed their wage bill was half that of Women’s Super League rivals Arsenal. United also spent far less on agent fees between February 2025 and 2026 than their competitors.

Asked whether the expectation on his team is too high given the gap in resources, Skinner gave a bullish response.

“I think we will learn from what investment is really needed to go into this level of competition for consistent years,” he said.

“I think we’re still learning as a club. I have incredible pressure, you know that, you read everything every day, sometimes you write it. I have incredible pressure and I hold that pressure. I want to say this, I’m incredibly proud of what my players are doing with the resources we have.

“Because we wear Manchester United’s badge, everybody expects us to be the very best team in the world. We have that expectation too. So that’s the pinch point, because we want to be the best. We’ve got to grow because we’re eight years old. We’re eight years old. You [can] give me all the flak, that’s fine, that’s no problem, that’s my job.

“But if we want to compete at this latter stage, we’ve seen what we’ve got to do, as a club. And then it’s our choice now, isn’t it? We have to look at what we seriously want to achieve and we’ll learn and grow from it. Even as a club, we’re still learning. It takes, sometimes, a punch in the face to wake up.”

United were without eight first-team players because of injury for this second leg but started strongly and deservedly took the lead after 11 minutes. Melvine Malard capitalised on a defensive error to finish into an empty net and bring her side level on aggregate.

News.title: Reeves backs North Sea drilling
News.content:
Rachel Reeves has backed drilling in the North Sea in a move that opens up a rift with Ed Miliband.

The Chancellor said she would be “very happy” to support extraction at two proposed new oil and gas fields because of the positive impact on “jobs and tax revenue”.

The intervention comes ahead of a decision by Mr Miliband, the Energy Secretary, on whether to grant licences for the Rosebank oil field and Jackdaw gas field.

Her comments put her on a collision course with Mr Miliband, who has banned new exploration in British waters and rejected pressure to extract more fossil fuels from the North Sea.

Asked if she supported drilling in the North Sea, Ms Reeves said: “I’m very happy that we are.”

“The North Sea oil and gas [will] play an important role in our energy mix for years to come, and we’re very lucky to have that resource and to be able to continue to use that resource.

“If we’re going to get ourselves off of this roller coaster of gas and oil prices, of course, we want to move to something that we have control over.”

It contrasts with Mr Miliband’s insistence that the only way to “get off the rollercoaster” is to abandon oil and gas altogether.

Meanwhile the SNP has u-turned on its opposition to further North Sea gas exploration in the aftermath of the war.

John Swinney, the First Minister of Scotland, said new fields should be permitted if the oil and gas they produced had a lower carbon footprint than imports.

The Chancellor’s comments come amid mounting pressure for Labour to reopen the North Sea as oil and gas prices surge as a result of the war in Iran.

Donald Trump urged the UK to “get your own oil” earlier this week and leading business figures including Octopus Energy boss Greg Jackson and British Gas chief Chris O’Shea have called for an expansion of North Sea drilling. Mr O’Shea said doing so “will bring prices down.”

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch this week launched a “get Britain drilling” campaign and Reform UK has also called for new North Sea exploration.

Ms Reeves told the BBC: “It would, of course, create jobs and tax revenue, and that is why we continue to support oil and gas for decades to come.

“We have now got the disruption in the Middle East, and it’s hard to get the oil and gas out of the Strait of Hormuz, which is pushing up prices. It does show that we have got to take control of our own energy supplies here in Britain.”

The Chancellor said the only reason drilling had not begun at Rosebank and Jackdaw was that courts overturned licenses granted by the previous government.

She said: “We said in our manifesto we would honor existing licenses, but the courts overturned the previous government’s decision. That is not the fault of this government, but we’ve had to go through the processes to be able to do it lawfully.”

Executives have said the fields could be producing fuel within months. Mr Miliband imposed new delay on the licence approval process by demanding new information from operators in recent weeks.

Ms Reeves also said she is “angry” that Donald Trump launched the Iran war without a “clear plan” in the most direct criticism of the president from a Cabinet minister yet.

She told the BBC: “I’m angry that Donald Trump has chosen to go to war in the Middle East – a war that there’s not a clear plan of how to get out of. It’s why we didn’t want to enter this.”

News.title: Water wars: the final escalation?
News.content:
But Iran is also acutely vulnerable to potential attacks on water infrastructure – its water system was already teetering on the brink of collapse before the war broke out.

After five years of extreme drought, the reservoirs supplying Tehran, a city of 17 million, were below 10 per cent capacity by late 2025, prompting the Iranian president to warn that the capital may need to be evacuated.

Now, under sustained bombardment and with sanctions preventing the import of spare parts and engineers, the country faces the real possibility of running out completely.

“The country is suffering from what I call a ‘water bankruptcy’ state,” said Prof Kaveh Madani, Director of the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health. “Water use has exceeded the sustainable or renewable supply for an extended period, to the point where some of the damage becomes irreversible.”

Rivers that once sustained farming and communities across Iran are now drying up, and groundwater reserves are being pumped out far faster than they can be replenished.

The Zayandeh Rud, which has irrigated the fields around Isfahan for centuries, has in recent years been reduced to a cracked plain of dried silt, while Lake Urmia, once the sixth largest lake in the world, has shrunk to less than a tenth of its former size.

For decades, Iranian development policies have been based on the assumption that engineering and extraction could overcome a vital shortage in the amount of water available.

While more than 600 large dams have been built, they have done little to compensate for the fact that there simply isn’t enough rain.

Annual rainfall has declined markedly in Iran, falling by around 20 per cent over the past two decades, according to the United Nations.

The UN now estimates that more than half of Iran’s population now lives in water-stressed areas.

Iran’s vulnerabilities in a water war would not be limited to its desalination plants, which provide only a small share of the country’s drinking water.

The dams, pumping stations and treatment works that its population of 88 million depend on for drinking water, agriculture and sanitation could all come under attack.

It would not be without precedent: throughout Middle Eastern history there have been numerous examples of water being weaponised.

Nebuchadnezzar II, the Babylonian king, is said to have destroyed the aqueduct supplying water to the city of Tyre in an attempt to end a 13-year siege in the sixth century BC.

In the 12th century, Saladin defeated a Crusader army by blocking their access to the Sea of Galilee and poisoning wells or filling them with sand.

More recently, in the 1960s, Arab states attempted to divert the waters of the Jordan River to prevent them from flowing into Israel’s National Water Carrier, sparking a series of confrontations that helped spark the Six-Day War.

During the first Gulf War, Saddam Hussein targeted Kuwaiti infrastructure, including power and water systems.

And in Ukraine, Russia has launched more than 100 attacks on water infrastructure since the war began in 2022, targeting dams, pumping stations and treatment works.

News.title: The 10 best yoga poses for beginners
News.content:
How long should you hold a yoga pose for?

Rather than timing you yoga pose, it’s best measured by breaths. As a beginner, aim for three to five breaths per yoga pose.

1. Iyengar

Best for: Beginners and those who like precision in their practice

Iyengar classes take a methodical approach to mastering yoga postures. “Classes include thorough demonstrations, a focus on proper alignment and the use of props to help you deepen your understanding of each posture and help with form,” explains Triyoga yoga manager Genny Wilkinson Priest. Purported benefits include developing strength and flexibility, helping with postural problems, and easing stress.

2. Ashtanga

Best for: Those who like the structure and discipline of a set routine

“A dynamic, breath-led practice, ashtanga follows a set series of poses,” explains Fi Clark, the head of yoga at FLY LDN. Think the likes of forward folds, shoulder stands and plenty of sun salutations. “It’s suitable from beginners up and comprises six series that increase in difficulty. Each series should be mastered before embarking on the next,” explains Clark. The benefits? “Ashtanga is good for building strength, flexibility, agility and mental focus.”

3. Vinyasa flow

Best for: People who like variety

“This form of yoga bares similarities to Ashtanga but incorporates more of a creative element to the sequences, allowing more freedom to be taught with different transitions and modifications,” says Clark. Often classes begin and end with a set of Ashtanga postures, with a more creative, flowing middle section where the teacher mixes it up, she explains. Many vinyasa classes are fast moving, so expect to get your sweat on.

4. Jivamukti

Best for: Those who want to experience the full 360-degree yogic package – not just a workout

With A-list models singing its praises, this form of yoga is seriously on-trend. But it’s not all about posturing and posing. “Jivamukti classes combine the physical, psychological and spiritual aspects of yoga,” says Wilkinson Priest. “Classes include vigorous asana [posture] practice, supported by Sanskrit chanting, music, readings and references to philosophical texts.”

5. Yin

Best for: Rebalancing the body and releasing tightness

Think slow. “Yin involves holding seated and lying down postures between two to five minutes,” explains Clark. If that seems a long old time don’t be put off – it’s all about simple, passive poses. “Yin roots itself in ancient practices linked to Chinese medicine. It’s believed we have thousands of meridians, or energy conduits, flowing through the body. If there are blockages, the body can’t function properly. Yin serves to clear those blockages,” explains Clark.

6. Hot yoga

Best for: Yoga fans who want to take it to the next level

As the name suggests, this is performed in a very warm, humid studio. There are multiple different kinds, the most well-known being Bikram. “Our Triyoga hot yoga classes follow a set sequence of postures designed to increase circulation, flexibility and strength,” says Wilkinson Priest. “The 36-38 degrees celsius heat penetrates the body deeply and warms muscles, while the increased blood flow makes them more pliable and ‘stretchy’.”

1. Leave your ego at the door

Yoga is not a competition. It’s not about who can stretch the furthest or the most complicated moves on your yoga mat. Practice self-compassion, and don’t compare yourself with others in the class.

2. You’re allowed to be bored

One of the meditation activities I’ve tried was to stare at a lit candle and allow the image of the flame to occupy my mind (also known as trataka). Afterwards, our instructor asked us how we felt – it’s supposed to help you find inner peace – but I just felt bored. This is fine and part of meditation. Strive for mental stillness.

3. Eat at least two hours before exercising

Don’t eat and flow. Just like any other form of exercise, make sure you leave two hours before eating. No one likes to feel their dinner swishing around, especially if you’re going to be holding downward dog for any length of time.

4. You may break wind

Don’t be ashamed, it happens. If you need to commiserate, just search #yogafarts on X. Worth noting: it seems to be some sort of unspoken rule of yoga that when you fart (or indeed, hear others) you shouldn’t do – or say – anything.

5. Check your leggings aren’t see-through

You want a pair that is practical, comfortable and not see-through - get a friend to be honest while you try downward dog. If you’re wearing shiny new leggings, you might want to invest in some liquid chalk for your feet, otherwise balancing your foot onto your opposite leg might be a bit of a slippery challenge.

News.title: How to spend the ultimate weekend in Las Vegas
News.content:
You'll spot it from far away, if you asked for a window seat on the plane. Welcome to Sin City – an oasis of glittering lights in the desert, home of the Strip and the drive-in wedding chapel, playground of the Mob, and a visual spectacle complete with its own Eiffel Tower, Egyptian pyramids and Venetian canals.

Las Vegas is a place that's defined as much by vintage camp as by futuristic innovation, where the 24-hour casinos exist alongside world-class dining, sleek hotels and thrilling entertainment, from the acrobatic stylings of Cirque du Soleil to the High Roller, a massive observation wheel. The nightlife is legendary, whether you're moving to the rhythm of DJ-spun beats on a dance floor lined with gold, or standing on an open-air terrace, drink in hand, taking in the sweeping views of neon-lit resorts and casinos below. This is Vegas, baby.

News.title: Grand National runners, favourites and odds for 2026: Key horses to note

News.title: I’m a Lego collector. These sets are the best for a screen-free Easter break
News.content:
No single Lego set is the perfect choice for everyone. I always recommend starting with a theme that best fits the interests of your intended recipient or your own tastes. This can include movies or TV shows such as Star Wars, Wicked, Bluey or Peppa Pig, or broader themes like space, animals or plants.

Each Lego set has a recommended age rating on the box. This dictates the size of the Lego bricks, as well as how complicated the build process is. If you’re buying for a young child, for example, it would be best to go for a Lego set with larger, less complex pieces and simple step-by-step instructions.

Calculating the ‘price per piece’ can also provide a good indication of each set’s value for money. This is simple: you just need to divide the total cost of the set by the number of pieces. Something to be mindful of is that licensed sets, such as Harry Potter and Star Wars, typically cost more per piece than Lego’s own themes.

Finally, if you time your purchase well, Lego can often be quite generous with its freebies. If you meet a spending threshold (£50, £75, £150 as examples,) the official Lego website might throw in some exclusive extras, so it’s always worth checking before you buy. My favourite in recent years was this tribute to Jane Austen’s books.

You also get points on every purchase on the Lego website with a Lego VIP membership, so it’s in your best interests to sign up.

Sports.title: Chelsea stars ‘unimpressed with Enzo Fernandez’ over Madrid bombshell as club icon tells him to ‘f*** off’ if not happy
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ’s recent antics have rubbed his Blues team-mates up the wrong way.

That is according to the Telegraph, who claim that his fellow stars have been left “unimpressed” by his conduct of late.





Fernandez is the vice-captain of Liam Rosenior‘s Chelsea side, and the acting leader while Reece James remains absent through injury.

But that has not stopped him making a series of nods to a potential summer transfer exit, with one European giant appearing to be his preferred destination.

The saga began with some reckless comments after Chelsea’s embarrassing 8-2 aggregate defeat to PSG last month, which saw them tumble out of the Champions League.

When asked after the match about a potential move in the summer, Fernandez told ESPN: “I don’t know, there are eight games left and the FA Cup. There’s the World Cup and then we’ll see.”



The lack of commitment, especially after such a significant defeat, put Chelsea fans on edge.

But many became truly frustrated with the midfielder – who arrived for a fee of £105million from Benfica in 2023 – when he began dropping hints about a specific destination he would love to live in one day.

He told Argentine outlet LuzuTV: “I always tell Valu that if I have to choose a city to live in Europe, I really like Madrid. It’s very similar to Buenos Aires.”

He also repeated similar sentiments during a stream with Argentine content creator Marcos Giles.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The Telegraph also claim that Fernandez has been increasingly vocal in the dressing room amid Chelsea’s torrid form, in which they have lost their last four games in all competitions.

He was even seen berating and even throwing a ball at keeper Filip Jorgensen after the Dane’s howler cost the Blues a shot at a comeback against PSG.

But it seems that behaviour is beginning to rub his colleagues the wrong way, especially in tandem with his attempts to leave the door open for a potential summer exit.



The current Chelsea squad are not the only stars who have had enough of the Argentine’s behaviour.

Iconic ex-Blues midfielder John Obi Mikel ripped into his conduct after the PSG defeat, and told him to “f*** off” if he is not committed to the team.

He said on his Obi One podcast: “You were the captain in that game and you come out and make those statements… How would that go down well with the senior players in the dressing room?

“For him to come out and make such a statement after we’ve been disgracefully dumped out of the Champions League, and you come out after wearing the captain’s armband…

“If he’s had enough, put your hands up, f*** off and we move on. No player is bigger than the football club, especially a club as huge as Chelsea.”



Mikel played 372 times for the West London outfit after arriving as a teenager.

He spent over a decade with the side, and is still as passionate about the club as the day he left.

He added: “You cannot come out and say that, it doesn’t matter what is going on.

“It doesn’t matter what is happening, you’re being paid handsomely to be at this football club, you should be grateful that you’re playing for a club like Chelsea.

“When you come out and make that statement, that is very, very disrespectful to the football club and to the fans.”

Sports.title: ‘Arteta likes him very much’ – Arsenal and Chelsea in transfer war for £87million striker, claims agent
Sports.content:
CHRISTIAN KOFANE’S agent has sensationally claimed that a host of top clubs are vying for his signature – and Arsenal are said to be in “pole position”.

Kofane, 19, has been making waves in Germany since breaking into the Bayer Leverkusen first team this season.





The teenage striker has scored seven goals and registered eight assists in 39 appearances for Leverkusen this term, and has already earned himself six senior caps for the Cameroon national team.

So it is no surprise that rumours are starting to swirl about a potential transfer in the summer.

According to his agent, Eric Depolo, Arsenal, Chelsea, Newcastle, Everton, Brentford, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are all keen on the forward.

But it’s the Gunners who are reportedly best placed to get a deal over the line as things stand.



In an interview with Daily Arsenal, it’s claimed Depolo said: “Arsenal’s interest is genuine. The manager [Mikel Arteta] likes him very much.

“I think it is too early to say [who is leading the race], but due to the fact that the player speaks Spanish, like Mikel Arteta, and that William Saliba is originally from Cameroon, I would say Arsenal are in pole position.”

Depolo also claimed that he has made contact with Arsenal about a potential move, but has valued his client at a whopping £87MILLION.

Sky Germany report that a deal for Kofane would likely cost between £52m and £61m, with Spanish giants Real Madrid also keeping tabs on the rising star.

Kofane has already impressed Arsenal fans with his showing against Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes in the first leg of Leverkusen’s Champions League last 16 tie against the Gunners.

Leverkusen manager Kasper Hjulmand waxed lyrical about Kofane’s performance in that first leg recently.

He said: “It is extremely difficult to take care of Kofane when he is in this form.

“He is strong, he delivers a lot in the pressing, he is present defensively, and he was a handful for the Arsenal centre-backs.”

Sports.title: Premier League giants set to boost capacity by up to 7,000 before end of season amid £300million stadium redevelopment
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY are set to complete a major redevelopment project at the Etihad.

City are gearing up for five key home games as they target Premier League and FA Cup glory after winning the Carabao Cup.





According to the Manchester Evening News, Man City are expecting to open the top tier of the North Stand up before the end of the season.

The Citizens are close to completing the first stage of their £300million redevelopment.

The plan is for more fans to be allowed in the ground, which currently attracts around 52,000 for homes games, before the end of the current campaign.

The new top tier will add another 7,000 seats at the Etihad, which will have a major effect on the ground’s atmosphere.

That will add more noise that can boost Pep Guardiola’s men in their bid to catch up on Premier League title rivals Arsenal, who top the table.

The Gunners are nine points ahead of the Manchester giants, who have a game in hand.

City will host the North Londoners in what could be a title decider on April 19.

Man City will also face Brentford and Aston Villa, while they also have a home game against Crystal Palace which was postponed.



The Citizens are scheduled to host Liverpool in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup on Saturday as well.

City, though, also have four away games scheduled in the Premier League.

Guardiola‘s side will travel to Chelsea, Burnley, Everton and Bournemouth.

Sports.title: KSI’s Dagenham and Redbridge takeover takes major twist as former Premier League club owner ‘buys huge stake’
Sports.content:
KSI has reportedly been joined by former Queens Park Rangers owner Tony Fernandes at Dagenham & Redbridge.

The YouTuber is understood to currently own about 20 per cent of the club after his arrival last month.





According to talkSPORT, the streamer-turned-amateur boxer has been followed by Fernandes, 61, who bought a 40 per cent stake.

This is a huge boost for Dagenham and the 32-year-old internet personality who is determined to lead the National League South side all the way to the Premier League.

The star owner wants to emulate Hollywood duo Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, who guided Wrexham from the National League to the Championship within a four-year period.

KSI recently said: “I want the place to be pumping, I want it to be rocking, I want it to be an event whenever you come here.

“Playing a video game and owning a football club is very different, I know that, but with Race to Division One [his FIFA YouTube series], it was a journey. It was hard, but in the end, I did it.

“With this club, I want to do the unthinkable. I want to take Dagenham and Redbridge to the Premier League.

“It’s obviously going to take time, but I’d say the realistic goal is getting out of this league and entering the National League.”

It seems like KSI will have a lot of experience by his side as Fernandes was a shareholder at QPR between 2011 and 2023.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Under the Malaysian businessman, the Rs spent a total of three years in the Premier League.

Fernandes bought the club just three months after they had secured promotion to the English top flight 15 years ago.

During his ownership, the club was twice relegated from the Prem despite avoiding the drop in his first season.

After dropping down to the Championship in 2013, QPR won promotion back to the top-flight at the first attempt a year later.

But the club suffered another relegation in the 2015/16 campaign and has since been in the Championship.



Fernandes will also be joining former Newcastle, Liverpool and West Ham star Andy Carroll at the board.

Carroll, 37, is also a minority shareholder and was placed as interim manager last month following the sacking of Lee Bradbury.

He exclusively told SunSport what it’s like working with KSI and how management just fell in his lap.

Sports.title: Darts star Luke Littler gives verdict on England flops after Japan defeat and reveals World Cup plan
Sports.content:
LUKE LITTLER is aiming to watch England live in the World Cup after helping them prepare for the tournament.

The World No1 had a throw with Thomas Tuchel’s stars last week, which included Phil Foden hitting a stunning 180.





It’s been two drab results for the Three Lions since but Littler, 19, is confident they can turn it around in two months time – and has plans to watch the clash with Panama.

He revealed: “Hopefully they do start winning. Next one now is the World Cup.

“I don’t think friendlies mean much. The players just need to keep fit and go back to their club and hopefully play well. I think we’ve still got a good chance in the World Cup.

“We play in New York [US Masters] on Thursday and Friday. Then England play the final group game against Panama on the Saturday.

“So hopefully we can make that, I checked. The actual ground is only 25 minutes away. So hopefully I can get to that one and sort some tickets.”

The world champion goes into his home Premier League in Manchester on Thursday night chasing a hat-trick of successive wins.



He faces Gian van Veen at the AO Arena having now won three out of the last four nights to storm to the top of the table.

Littler now reckons that some players, like in the days of Phil Taylor’s dominance, have lost before even throwing a dart against him.

Sports.title: Tottenham legend gives verdict on Roberto De Zerbi’s masterplan to save Spurs from relegation nightmare
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM legend Jermain Defoe has backed Roberto De Zerbi’s “wow football” to keep Spurs in the Prem.

De Zerbi was handed the reins at Tottenham this week with the club 17th in the table and one point above the relegation places.





The Italian has seven games to save Spurs from the drop, starting with a trip to Sunderland next week.

But Defoe, who scored 143 goals in 363 appearances for Tottenham, is confident De Zerbi is up to the task.

The former Spurs striker said: “He is someone that comes in with an unbelievable CV.

“When you look at his playing style, as football fans, you have to appreciate and enjoy the way they play.



“I remember that Brighton team, watching Brighton play, and thinking: ‘Wow, this is the right way to play football’.

“He is going into a massive football club. But he is someone with a good CV and someone who backs himself.

“I just hope this group of players can respond to that and just get the results that they need.

“A lot of the players haven’t experienced this before. The fans and the club have not been through this situation before.

“So, hopefully they can come out of it. And with his manager, I’m sure he’s good enough to get the results they need.”

Defoe, 43, retired from playing four years ago and followed that up by working as a coach in Spurs’ academy.

The ex striker has now taken the plunge into management, though, and has his first game in charge of Woking on Friday.

BRISTOL CITY have revealed grand plans to build a stunning new centre for its foundation.

The Robins confirmed that an application has been sent in for work at Filwood Playing Fields in the south of the city.





The area is around two miles away from the club’s Ashton Gate stadium with the project aiming to “create new opportunities for local people of all ages and backgrounds”.

Perennial Championship outfit City – who recently appointed veteran manager Roy Hodgson to see out the season – will base their Robins Foundation at the Sports and Education Hub.

They have promised to upgrade the outdoor space with improved grass pitches, two artificial ones and a multi-use games area.

Concept images looking from a new car park show a modern building design with high, panelled windows.

The club’s white and red colours fade into each other on a futuristic blocky exterior.

It is said that the space will be accessible for the wider community to use.

The club also released plans for another multi-use pitch and Cruyff Court – a special five-a-side pitch – to be included.

Play areas for children have also been listed on the blueprint with an indoor sports hall and classrooms once you enter.

There will also be room for conferences, functions and a cafe.

City add that it will have a new clubhouse for Mendip Broadwalk Football Club.

They opened their glossy High Performance Centre training ground just outside Failand in 2021 and are aiming to finally get into the Premier League.

City had looked to be promotion contenders under Gerhard Struber but he was sacked after falling down the table in 2026.

Hodgson, 78, is now tasked with steering them to safety and avoiding a late-season relegation battle.



They have never been in the Prem and are based in the biggest city in England to not host a top flight game since its rebrand in 1992.

They have now been in the Championship for 11 years, finishing between 19th and sixth.

They made the play-offs last term but have hit rocky form of late and are stranded once again.

Sports.title: England star insists drab World Cup preparation let-down is 'not the end of the world'
Sports.content:
England star insists drab World Cup preparation let-down is 'not the end of the world'

Aston Villa defender believes the disappointing double-header at Wembley will have no negative impact on England's preparations for the World Cup this summer

View 3 Images Konsa has shrugged off England's uninspiring World Cup preparation (Image: Getty Images)

Ezri Konsa followed the script after England’s so-called Send-Off Series turned out to be the least inspiring farewell imaginable. “It’s not the end of the world,” said the Aston Villa defender after the limpest of Wembley defeats to a tidy Japan team that tired badly in the closing stages.

‌



“There is always going to be noise outside. We’ve got to make sure we stick together as a team, and that is something we have done.”

‌



It might not be the end of the world but the draw with Uruguay and the loss to Japan should have at least given Thomas Tuchel plenty to mull over before selecting his final squad for the World Cup. And England’s central defensive combinations should be on the manager’s agenda.

‌



Arsenal news: Gunners sent warning about 11 international break injuries as Ben White called out READ MORE :

“I don’t think I’m cemented in there,” said Konsa. “I don’t take it for granted. I have to make sure I keep working, keep improving.

“There is a lot of competition, a lot of top class centre-halves. I have to make sure I go back and stay consistent for the last two months.”

But assuming he is fit, Konsa IS ‘cemented in there’. In fact, ahead of the forgettable Uruguay-Japan double, the only question was whether or not he would start England’s first game.

‌



Marc Guehi, skipper against Japan, looks a certainty, with either Konsa or John Stones as his partner. But in the eyes of most observers, Harry Maguire made a very decent international comeback, even though Tuchel was not particularly effusive about the Manchester United man.

View 3 Images Harry Maguire made an impressive comeback to the international arena (Image: PA)

For the last ten minutes of the Japan game, though, the England boss did send on Maguire and Dan Burn - his version of a rugby bomb squad. And the pair caused Japan problems.

‌



“It’s always good to have that. Set pieces are really important,” said Konsa. “If it works, it works. For us, that is the main thing.”

When discussing his central defensive options, Tuchel has also given a positive name-check to Trevor Chalobah and also has Fikayo Tomori as an option. And even though Tuchel must have a fair idea of the make-up of his final squad, the next few weeks of club football could still have an impact on his selection, particularly in the centre-half area.

“So many players at the moment are playing for so many trophies and fighting for so many things,” said Guehi after the Japan reverse. “So it is important we leave this where it is and pick it up when it’s time.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has plenty mull over after the Wembley loss to Japan

"You can’t be thinking about one thing when you are doing another. I think it’s important we go back to our clubs and make sure we are ready.”

Konsa agreed, adding: “Everyone is gonna go back, focus on club football and when we meet up in the summer, we’re going to make sure that we are fully prepared for what is to come. We wanted to win these games - unfortunately we didn’t.

Article continues below

"We played against very good teams and I’m sure the boss knows what he’s doing. We will go into pre-camp before the World Cup, play another two friendlies and make sure we are fully prepared.”

Viktor Gyokeres scored a dramatic late winner for Sweden against Poland on Tuesday night, and the Arsenal striker will now turn his attentions back to the Premier League title race

View 2 Images The next few weeks will be crucial for Viktor Gyokeres and Arsenal in the title run‑in (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Viktor Gyokeres knows he must now refocus his attention on Arsenal after firing Sweden to World Cup qualification, netting an 88th‐minute winner in a thrilling 3-2 triumph over Poland on Tuesday night. The frontman was perfectly positioned to sweep home the all-important third goal.

‌



However, thoughts will quickly shift back to Arsenal as he returns to north London, with Mikel Arteta's side entering a pivotal run-in ahead of the final day of the season on 24 May. Any stumble between now and then could prove devastating in their quest to end their lengthy Premier League title wait.

‌



Manchester City sit nine points adrift, though they possess a game in hand against Crystal Palace. Victory for Pep Guardiola's men would trim the deficit to six points and, as football has repeatedly demonstrated, even a commanding lead can vanish rapidly should Arsenal start dropping points.

"That was me, especially at the end when we had some half-dangerous chances. We believed in it until the end and that is why we are in the World Cup.

"We believed in it until the end and that is why we are in the World Cup."

Sports.title: Man City seek out Pep Guardiola for contract decision as ideal timeline set
Sports.content:
Man City seek out Pep Guardiola for contract decision as ideal timeline set

Pep Guardiola's Manchester City future continues to remain a major talking point with the Catalan linked with a summer exit despite having a contract until 2027

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola continues to be linked with a Man City exit (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City have formally sought out Pep Guardiola to see whether he plans to see out his contract - or leave once this current season ends.

‌



The Catalan is in his tenth season at the helm but noise continues to swirl that this could prove to be his swansong at the Etihad. Guardiola has just claimed another trophy in the form of the Carabao Cup, which saw City down title rivals Arsenal at Wembley.

‌



After that triumph TalkSPORT understands that senior figures at the club attempted to gauge whether Guardiola was planning to stay put in the summer, or call it a day. Even the likes of sporting director Hugo Viana still don't know whether the 55-year-old will remain in his post come the end of this season.

‌



City had hoped that Guardiola would confirm, at least privately, whether or not he was staying during this international break. The club need to prepare for all scenarios, the worst of which leaves them needing a new manager.

Guardiola has always been allowed the right to make up his own mind about his future and the club maintain they have contingency plans in place should Guardiola leave a year before his contract expires.

Former Premier League star has wild World Cup nightclub celebration with arm in a sling READ MORE :

Gianluigi Donnarumma speaks out with emotional statement after Italy World Cup failure READ MORE :

It is understood that several summer targets, including Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, are keen to know whether or not Guardiola will be the manager before making the decision. However there is no suggestion players will turn down City's approaches should the Catalan no longer be in charge.

‌



One man to previously be linked with the job if Guardiola were to leave was Enzo Maresca, who was axed by Chelsea on New Year's Day. The Italian previously served as an assistant to the Catalan and admitted that he held talks with figures at the club about a future role.

View 2 Images Man City's hierarchy are having to consider the possibility that Pep Guardiola opts to leave (Image: Getty Images)

Guardiola has won 19 trophies at the Etihad, including six Premier League titles and the Champions League in 2023. He's in the midst of rebuilding his side and is seeking to avoid going successive years without claiming the top flight.

‌



The City boss has continued investing in his squad with the likes of Marc Guehi, Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Tijjani Reijnders joining in the last 12 months. The Manchester outfit trail league leaders Arsenal by nine points but do have a game in hand.

Guardiola and City recently downed the Gunners and will face them later this month, which could see them cut the gap at the top.

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe 'can't expect to jump in at the top' after bagging Woking gig
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe 'can't expect to jump in at the top' after bagging Woking gig

Jermain Defoe has been named the new manager of Woking but has no issues beginning his management journey in non-league, despite an impressive Premier League career

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe has dropped down to the National League to land his first managerial job

Jermain Defoe has stepped into the world of management after landing the Woking job and knows he "can't expect to just jump in at the top" as he begins life in the National League.

‌



The former Tottenham and West Ham striker has been doing his education having held coaching roles at the likes of Rangers, but has gone out on his own and will look to have an impact in non-league with the Surrey-based outfit.

‌



The former England striker was announced as Woking's new boss, replacing Neal Ardley, on Sunday. Defoe played with the Three Lions with the likes of Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Wayne Rooney. All men who have seen their playing careers open doors for them.

‌



Gerrard landed an early managerial role at Rangers whilst Lampard's second job was at Chelsea. Defoe hasn't been afforded those luxuries but never expected his prior achievements to make a difference.

He said: "My mum's always said to me in life, you've got to be grateful for every opportunity you get. Everyone's journey is different. You look at successful managers, everyone's journey has been different.

Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition READ MORE :

"It's important to appreciate the opportunity. When I was a player, a young 16-year-old at West Ham in the youth team, you have to earn your stripes. You have to do your apprenticeship. You can't expect, just because I've had a good career, I can't expect to just jump in at the top or get that big job."

‌



Defoe is now just one of only five black managers in the top five tiers of English football. That has long been cited as an issue that needs addressing - and the Woking boss hopes to see it rise sooner rather than later. "It's something that's been spoken about for many years," he said.

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe scored 162 times in the Premier League

"I remember as a player, all the different campaigns and speaking to the likes of Les Ferdinand, Ian Wright, Andy Cole - that generation before me who did their coaching badges and obviously there was a lack of opportunities.

‌



"I would like to think going forward, other black managers now will get opportunities. Players that are still playing, hopefully in the future, they'll get opportunities. I think there's always going to be expectation on any manager at any level. You're a manager of a football club that has to win."

Woking drew with Altrincham on Tuesday with interim boss Craig Ross in charge. They are 10th in the table, 11 points off the play-offs with six matches of the season remaining.

Sports.title: Gianluca Prestianni speaks out on Vinicius racism row - 'I was punished without evidence'
Sports.content:
Gianluca Prestianni speaks out on Vinicius racism row - 'I was punished without evidence'

Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni has continued to maintain his innocence regarding the alleged racial slur he said to Real Madrid's Vinicius Jnr, which saw him banned by UEFA

View 2 Images Gianluca Prestianni insists he was punished for something he "never did" (Image: (Joao Bravo/Sports Press Photo/Getty Images))

Gianluca Prestianni has hit out at the punishment he faced from UEFA for an alleged racial slur aimed at Vinicius Jnr - insisting that he was "punished without any evidence".

‌



The Benfica star was prevented from playing in the second-leg of his side's Champions League last 16 tie with Real Madrid. That was due to a comment he is alleged to have made in the direction of Los Blancos' Brazilian forward.

‌



Real would win 3-1 on aggregate but the first-leg was overshadowed by an unsavoury incident. Vinicius reported to the referee that Prestianni had used a racial slur after he had opened the scoring, which saw him booked for his celebrations.

‌



The Benfica player publicly denied the allegations afterwards, claiming his opponent had "misinterpreted" what he'd said. UEFA suspended the Argentine for the game at the Bernabeu and could yet ban him for 10 matches if found guilty.

But Prestianni has spoken candidly about the incident and feels as though the backlash he received wasn't warranted, especially as he continues to protest his innocence.

Benfica handed punishment by UEFA after racism incident during Real Madrid clash READ MORE :

Jose Mourinho breaks silence after criticism over Vinicius Junior incident with Benfica vow READ MORE :

He said in an interview with Telefe: "What really hurt me was being treated for something I never did. That hurt me more than anything else. But fortunately, I am very calm, because everyone who knows me knows the kind of person I am, and that is enough for me."

‌



Prestianni also went on to say: “I am very grateful to the club (Benfica) that believed in me and supported me throughout this journey. The club and my teammates have shown this support internally, and that means much more to me than simply posting a story on Instagram.”

View 2 Images The Benfica star was accused of making a racist comment to Vinicius Jr (Image: Getty Images)

The Benfica star thanked the club for sticking by him, but maintained he was reprimanded despite there being no evidence again him. “It hurt me a lot," he confessed. "I was punished without any evidence for something I didn’t say. But it’s over now. I am very grateful to the Benfica staff who waited until the last moment to include me (in the second leg).”

‌



Benfica boss Jose Mourinho landed himself in hot water over the incident when he suggested that Vinicius' celebration had incited the reaction, whilst also making comments about his history regarding racial slurs.

He said: "When you score a goal like that, you celebrate in a respectful way." The Special One also added: "There is something wrong because it happens in every stadium. Every stadium that Vinicius plays [in] something happens. Always."

Sports.title: Former Premier League star has wild World Cup nightclub celebration with arm in a sling
Sports.content:
Former Premier League star has wild World Cup nightclub celebration with arm in a sling

Bosnia & Herzegovina made history, defeating Italy in a dramatic penalty shootout to secure their place in the 2026 World Cup.

View 2 Images

Former Manchester City striker Edin Dzeko led jubilant celebrations with the Bosnia & Herzegovina squad after they secured a dramatic World Cup qualification. The team triumphed over Italy in Zenica, winning 4-1 in a penalty shoot-out following a 1-1 draw after extra time.

‌



This marks Bosnia's second-ever World Cup appearance, the first since Brazil 2014. Despite suffering a shoulder injury in the final seconds of extra time after being hacked down by Davide Frattesi and receiving treatment, Dzeko battled through the full 120 minutes but was unable to take part in the shootout.

‌



He watched from the sidelines with his arm in a sling. Bosnia coach Sergej Barbarez said afterwards: I hope that it is not a great injury to Edin Dzeko and that he will be able to be with us at the World Cup because he does not have much time."

‌



Defiant Thomas Tuchel unwavering in World Cup belief despite underwhelming send-off READ MORE :

England superfan opens about selling house to fund 10th World Cup trip and early retirement READ MORE :

That didn't stop the 40-year-old from partying through the night, dancing and singing in a bar. He later shared footage on Instagram, showing the squad enjoying their historic achievement.

He also shared photos from the packed streets of Sarajevo, where the Bosnia squad celebrated atop a rooftop bus surrounded by thousands of fans.

View 2 Images Thousands of fans gathered the streets of Bosnia

‌



Despite being unable to take a penalty for his country, the striker said it felt like destiny.

"I keep saying it must have been fate, for it to happen in the last second of the match, and then for me not to be able to take a penalty," he said.

"Someone else stepped up instead of me, scored, and in the end we won. Who knows, maybe if I had taken it, I wouldn't have scored, so it all feels like it comes from above."

‌

On his arm injury, Dzeko added: "We're all relieved about the arm, it's not the worst case scenario. Most likely it won't need surgery.

"So I hope that in maybe a month, month and a half, I should be back."

‌



Bosnia moved into Group B, where they will face Canada, Qatar and Switzerland in the tournament across the United States, Mexico and Canada.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition

Phil Foden deputised for Harry Kane during England's defeat by Japan but his struggles in that game, and more widely, could leave him as the Three Lions' big World Cup casualty

View 2 Images Foden struggled during England's friendlies against Uruguay and Japan (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel has delivered a brutal World Cup warning to Phil Foden. Tuchel admitted Foden is “not guaranteed” a place in England’s squad because he is clearly “struggling” on the pitch.

‌



Manchester City forward Foden is in serious danger of being the biggest casualty this summer because he is out of form for club and country.

‌



Foden, 25, who has won 49 caps, started England’s final Wembley warm-up friendlies with Uruguay and Japan but was substituted before the hour mark in both games.

‌



England boss Tuchel insists that Foden was excellent in training and in camp but admitted that he failed to live up to expectations on the pitch.

Tuchel said: “He tried everything. I would say he was excellent in camp but, yeah, he struggles to show it on the pitch. Obviously he didn’t have a lot of minutes for City recently.

“Then he came to camp with the brightest smile and was so good in training and I thought he will just surprise us and will play with the same verve and excitement but, yeah, he struggles to have the full impact.”

‌



Tuchel was then asked whether he can actually take a player to the World Cup who is struggling on the pitch. “I can, I can! The question will be if we will,” admitted Tuchel.

That clearly put major doubt on Foden’s inclusion and Tuchel admitted: “Well, it’s not a guarantee that he will come.”

Foden went to Euro 2024 on the back of the season of his life but failed to deliver his best performances and since then has struggled with form and fitness.

‌



He has made 26 Premier League appearances for City this season - including five as a substitute - and managed seven goals and three assists.

View 2 Images Foden's spot on the plane is at risk (Image: Getty Images)

But Foden is no longer a guaranteed starter at City and is also facing huge competition for England as Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer are all in the mix for a place as No10. Eberechi Eze is another who could fit into that role.

‌



It looks certain that Tuchel will have to leave at least one of the big names at home this summer - and increasingly it looks like Foden is most at risk.

But Tuchel has insisted that he has taken valuable lessons from the two friendlies - even though they failed win either and lost to Japan.

Tuchel added: “I learn all the time. I learn from every training session and I learn from how the squad is together and I learn from the players react to the game plan and how they adapt.

Article continues below

“How quick they can learn and how quick they can adapt and how they can put it on the pitch. Everything is a learning.”

Sports.title: Defiant Thomas Tuchel unwavering in World Cup belief despite underwhelming send-off
Sports.content:
Defiant Thomas Tuchel unwavering in World Cup belief despite underwhelming send-off

Thomas Tuchel watched his England side labour to a draw against Uruguay and a defeat by Japan but insists his belief that the Three Lions can win he World Cup is undiminished

View 2 Images England boss Thomas Tuchel

Thomas Tuchel insists he still “100 per cent believes” in his England squad even after their rude awakening. England are one of the bookies’ favourites to win the World Cup and are fourth seeds in the tournament’s tennis-style draw system.

‌



But England were brought crashing back down to earth in their final Wembley warm-up friendlies with Uruguay and Japan which raised some serious doubts.

‌



England look half the team without Harry Kane. There was no Jude Bellingham to save them. They have yet to beat a team in the top 20 under Tuchel. The draw with Uruguay was flat. The defeat to Japan was a serious wake-up call.

‌



But despite the two chastening results, Tuchel insists that his confidence in his team has not wavered. England had a 100 per cent record in qualifying without even conceding a goal.

Thomas Tuchel issues bleak World Cup warning to Phil Foden after failed England audition READ MORE :

Tuchel said: “I’m still believing 100 per cent. Like I said, I knew we will have a tough exam, and sometimes it is better to have a tough exam than another win and we’re not so 100 per cent sure. We will not start doubting now.

“It is difficult also for the players to come to camp, then they hear my voice for the first time, see our principles for the first time, have an offensive session, defensive session, and then go and show in Wembley. Not easy.

‌



“We will put this into perspective, but on the other side, we have built something in September, October and November, and we will rely on that.

“We opened the doors again, to see players, to give them the chance, to have a full impression and not only from the tribune.

“So to feel the players, have them in training, see what they are capable of, see what they are struggling with, and then learn from there, take the consequences, and build a team for June.”

‌



Tuchel’s split squad - naming 35 players for the two games and giving 11 of them the first week off - was designed to give them a break and also look at some fresh faces.

Everton’s James Garner impressed against Uruguay. Harry Maguire did himself a power of good. Marcus Rashford was also a big winner as he played well in the first game and came on and made a difference against Japan.

Ben White was hero and villain against Uruguay and, while he struggled against Japan, it no longer looks impossible for him to go to the World Cup.

‌



Dom Solanke and Dominic Calvert-Lewin probably feel as if they could have done more to push their claims to be Kane’s deputy. Maybe there is a slot still there for Ollie Watkins.

View 2 Images Ben White had an eventful international break (Image: Alex Davidson - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

So it was ultimately hit and miss for Tuchel’s March camp and he admitted that his biggest disappointment was not getting a winning send-off but insists they will not drop their heads.

‌



“Like I said, we will not let go of our dream, not let go of the question ‘Why not?’” said Tuchel.

“Now the most important thing is that the players reintegrate with their clubs, have a good end to the season, and then we have them in pre-camp and prepare them properly and take steps from there.”

The biggest danger now to England’s chances is surely burnout. Too many games, the demands of the Premier League which saw the likes of Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice withdraw with knocks.

‌



But Tuchel says he has a plan to ensure that the players will start the World Cup feeling fresh as he wants the pre-camp in Florida - which features friendlies against New Zealand and Costa Rica - to feel like a mini holiday with families welcomed in.

Tuchel added: “They will get a week off, the guys who are not involved in the Champions League final. And then we will go very early to the US, earlier than maybe other teams. But we will go there to prepare us for the heat and the humidity.

“But we will have an early camp also that allows us a good mix between free time and also family-friends time, and football, to arrive with excitement when the tournament starts.

Article continues below

“The season is a long, long season this year for the players, because some of them come from the Club World Cup, and it will not end in the end of May. It will end, hopefully, in the middle of July. And we will take this into account.”

Sports.title: Bompastor rages again on VAR: What are they doing in these games?
Sports.content:
Sonia Bompastor once again took aim at VAR after the system did not review a Katie McCabe hair pull on Alyssa Thompson for a red card - with the Chelsea boss instead being booked and then sent off.

Bompastor received her first yellow card for her angry protests after McCabe was not penalised late in the game, shouting at the referee as the card was brandished. VAR would have looked at the incident and, with no review, clearly did not see an issue with the on-field decision.

Then less than a minute later, Bompastor encroached on the pitch as she tried to quickly retrieve the ball for her side, and was shown a red card following a second booking.

While she said little about whether she deserved to be sent off, she was adamant that VAR should have checked the hair-pulling incident, once again questioning the use of the technology in the women's game after similar comments made after the first leg.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anton Toloui reflects on Chelsea being dumped out of the Women's Champions League by London rivals Arsenal.

Image: Bompastor shouts at referee Frida Klarlund, earning a yellow card, which was followed by a second

"In the moment, I was emotional because I think it's clear for everyone," Bompastor said.

"I can probably understand the referees sometimes can't see that, but I don't understand - and it's not been the first time now - why the VAR is not checking that situation?

"Why are they not going back to that, checking and having a clear call on that? Because the impact on my player she was emotional.

Image: Bompastor watched the final moments of the Women's Champions League quarter-final through the side of the tunnel

"At the end, I'm the one who gets a red card, where I think the Arsenal player should be the one who gets a red card.

"What is the VAR doing in these games? If we have the VAR, why are we not checking these situations? I don't understand, and it's not good enough."

She added to BBC Sport that Thompson had been upset by the incident, saying: "She was crying.

"She's trying her best on the pitch in both games and it is not good enough. When you are playing football and someone pulls your hair, it's bad. She was emotional with that situation and the result."

However, McCabe said on social media that her hair pull had not been intentional, posting: "I just want to clarify that I was genuinely reaching for the shirt, I wouldn't ever want to pull someone's hair. Full respect to Thompson."

White: It looked cynical Former WSL striker Ellen White on BBC Sport:



"I was really shocked that VAR didn't send the referee to review it and have a look. It does look very cynical.



"We've seen it before with a hair pull and it's a straight red card, so it has to go to review.



"We don't know if it could have had an impact but there was a minute to go and Thompson was flying down that wing. Could she have crossed the ball in and [Chelsea] have scored? Could it have gone to extra-time? We don't know.



"If it was pulled back and reviewed and McCabe got a red card then Chelsea have a free-kick with Arsenal down to 10. Anything could have happened."

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers added: "I have seen the still picture back. I didn't see the incident on the pitch when it was happening but I did see Katie going to Alyssa to apologise. My assumption is it's not intentional but it is of course unlucky. I have to watch it back before I comment more."

Bompastor also went further to point out how the referee Frida Klarlund and VAR official Katrin Rafalski had previously made mistakes in the Champions League.

"The referee who was refereeing the game was the one who, two years ago for Chelsea, didn't allow the ball for offside, but it was onside," she said.

"I think she was the one who also gave a penalty kick to Real Madrid, and the foul was outside the box.

Image: Bompastor reacts after being shown a yellow card by referee Klarlund

"And the one who was doing the VAR was the one who disallowed our goal against Barcelona when [Catarina] Macario scored and that goal was onside.

"So I'm just questioning, why are these referees coming into this game with what happened in the first leg, refereeing these games? I don't think that's good enough.

"I'm really frustrated and upset, but not only for me, but my players deserve more respect for the performance they put on the pitch."

It was a chaotic end to the all-WSL Women's Champions League quarter-final tie, which Arsenal won 3-2 on aggregate despite Chelsea's 1-0 win on the night.

The Gunners will face either Lyon or Wolfsburg in the semi-finals which begin at the end of April. The two European heavyweights meet in their second leg on Thursday evening.

Sports.title: Woods will not captain US team at 2027 Ryder Cup
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has told the PGA of America he will not captain the US Ryder Cup team in 2027, following his decision to take a break from golf after his car crash.

The decision announced on Wednesday by the PGA of America was expected considering recent developments involving Woods.

He was arrested Friday on suspicion of driving under the influence during a car crash near his home in South Florida. Woods entered a plea of not guilty on Tuesday and posted a statement later that said he was stepping away indefinitely.

"This is necessary in order for me to prioritize my well-being and work toward lasting recovery," he said in a social media post.

Prior to his car crash, Woods was the favourite to lead the US team in next year's matches at Adare Manor in Ireland.

"The PGA of America stands in full support of Tiger Woods as he steps away to focus on his health and well-being," the association's statement read. "During this time, we are keeping Tiger in our thoughts and prayers, with sincere hope for his strength, comfort, and recovery."

It added: "Tiger has shared with us that he will not serve as captain of the 2027 US Ryder Cup team and we support his decision. The PGA of America will share further updates regarding the Ryder Cup captaincy when appropriate."

Luke Donald was announced last month as Europe's Ryder Cup captain for the third consecutive term.

Ryder Cup-winning captain Paul McGinley believes people are running out of patience with Woods as he is in the "last-chance saloon" in terms of his golfing career.

McGinley, who is part of Sky Sports' coverage of next week's Masters, said it was unlikely the 50-year-old Woods would win a tournament on any of the main tours again and would be better suited to enhancing his current administrative role as chairman of the PGA Tour's Future Competition Committee.

Woods remained optimistic of challenging for another major victory during his most recent appearance at Augusta National in 2024, only to card a third-round 82 - the worst round of his major career as a professional - and finish last of those who made the weekend.

"I think a lot of people are hanging on thinking like that [him contending again]," former Ryder Cup player Andrew Coltart told Sky Sports News. "The man's into his fifties now. He's seen it all, he's done it all.

"It's like watching the old boxing champions, the legends of old, returning to the ring when really their body has just been through absolutely everything. I don't think we're ever going to see that [him challenge] again, but let's be fair to him - everybody's allowed to get old!"
